sources.title: Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Besin yakıtımızdır; besin öğeleri hücrelere çalışmak için gereken enerjiyi ve maddeleri verir; ama önce vücudun emip kullanabileceği küçük parçalara sindirilmelidir.
facts.quote: Food is our fuel, and its nutrients give our bodies' cells the energy and substances they need to work. / But before food can do that, it must be digested into small pieces the body can absorb and use.

facts.statement: Sindirim sistemi besin öğelerini vücudun emip enerji için kullanabileceği kadar küçük parçalara ayırır.
facts.quote: Your digestive system breaks nutrients into parts small enough for your body to absorb and use for energy
facts.location: NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Sindirim ağızda, besin mideye ulaşmadan çok önce başlar; dişler besini koparıp doğrar, tükürük onu ıslatır; tükürüğü tükürük bezleri yapar.
facts.quote: Digestion begins in the mouth, well before food reaches the stomach. / As the teeth tear and chop the food, spit moistens it for easy swallowing. / Your salivary glands make saliva, a digestive juice
facts.location: Nemours KidsHealth — Your Digestive System; NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Tükürükteki amilaz adlı sindirim enzimi bazı karbonhidratları parçalamaya başlar; tükürükteki enzim nişastaları parçalamaya başlar.
facts.quote: A digestive enzyme in saliva called amylase (AH-meh-lace) starts to break down some of the carbohydrates / Saliva also has an enzyme that begins to break down starches in your food.
facts.location: Nemours KidsHealth — Your Digestive System; NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Yemeği koklamak ya da düşünmek bile ağzı sulandırabilir; beyin tükürük bezlerine sinyal gönderir.
facts.quote: Just by smelling that homemade apple pie or thinking about how delicious that ripe tomato is going to be / your brain sends a signal that causes your salivary glands to "make your mouth water" to prepare you to eat.
facts.location: Nemours KidsHealth — Your Digestive System; NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Yutarken dil besini boğaza iter; epiglot denen küçük doku kapağı boğulmayı önlemek için soluk borusunun üstüne kapanır.
facts.quote: When you swallow, your tongue pushes the food into your throat. / A small flap of tissue, called the epiglottis, folds over your windpipe to prevent choking
facts.location: NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Peristalsis denen kas kasılma dalgaları besini yemek borusundan mideye iter.
facts.quote: Waves of muscle contractions called peristalsis (per-uh-STALL-sus) force food down through the esophagus to the stomach.

facts.statement: Yemek borusunun sonundaki sfinkter genelde kapalı durur ve mide içeriğinin yemek borusuna geri akmasını engeller.
facts.quote: This sphincter usually stays closed to keep what’s in your stomach from flowing back into your esophagus.
facts.location: NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Mide kasları besini asit ve enzim içeren sindirim sıvılarıyla çalkalayıp karıştırır; mide duvarındaki bezler mide asidi ve enzim yapar; midedeki sindirim için asitli ortam gerekir.
facts.quote: The stomach muscles churn and mix the food with digestive juices that have acids and enzymes / Glands in your stomach lining make stomach acid and enzymes that break down food. / An acidic environment is needed for the digestion that takes place in the stomach.
facts.location: Nemours KidsHealth — Your Digestive System; NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Mide, kimus denen içeriğini yavaş yavaş ince bağırsağa boşaltır; midenin çıkışındaki ceviz büyüklüğündeki pilor kapağı kimusu midede tutar.
facts.quote: The stomach slowly empties its contents, called chyme, into your small intestine. / A walnut-sized muscular valve at the outlet of the stomach called the pylorus (pie-LOR-us) keeps chyme in the stomach
facts.location: NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works; Nemours KidsHealth — Your Digestive System

facts.statement: İnce bağırsağa uzunluğu yüzünden değil genişliği yüzünden ince denir; aslında kalın bağırsaktan çok daha uzundur.
facts.quote: The small intestine is called small because of its width, not its length. It's actually much longer than the large intestine.

facts.statement: İnce bağırsağın iç duvarı milyonlarca mikroskobik, parmak gibi villus ile kaplıdır; besinler villuslar aracılığıyla kana emilir; ince bağırsak duvarları suyu ve sindirilmiş besinleri kana emer.
facts.quote: The inner wall of the small intestine is covered with millions of microscopic, finger-like projections called villi (VIH-lie). / The villi are the vehicles through which nutrients can be absorbed into the blood. / The walls of the small intestine absorb water and the digested nutrients into your bloodstream.
facts.location: Nemours KidsHealth — Your Digestive System; NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: İnce bağırsağın kasları besini pankreas, karaciğer ve bağırsaktan gelen sindirim sıvılarıyla karıştırır; karaciğer yağların sindirimine yardım eden safrayı yapar; safra kesesi safrayı öğünler arasında saklar; pankreas karbonhidrat, yağ ve proteinleri parçalayan enzimler yapar.
facts.quote: The muscles of the small intestine mix food with digestive juices from the pancreas, liver, and intestine / Your liver makes a digestive juice called bile that helps digest fats and some vitamins. / Your gallbladder stores bile between meals. / Your pancreas makes a digestive juice that has enzymes that break down carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.
facts.location: NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Kalın bağırsak suyu emer ve atığı sıvıdan katı dışkıya dönüştürür.
facts.quote: The large intestine absorbs water and changes the waste from liquid into stool. / The large intestine's main job is to remove water from the undigested matter and form solid waste (poop) to be excreted.
facts.location: NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works; Nemours KidsHealth — Your Digestive System

facts.statement: Kalın bağırsaktaki bakteriler kalan besin öğelerini parçalamaya yardım eder ve K vitamini yapar.
facts.quote: Bacteria in your large intestine help break down remaining nutrients and make vitamin K.
facts.location: NIDDK (NIH) — Your Digestive System & How It Works

facts.statement: Bir yetişkinin sindirim kanalı yaklaşık 9 metre uzunluğundadır.
facts.quote: An adult's digestive tract is about 30 feet (about 9 meters) long.

facts.statement: Vücudun besini tamamen sindirmesi saatler sürer.
facts.quote: It takes hours for our bodies to fully digest food.
